# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

I found no blockers. The rule is correct, the second commit fixes the byte-write bug from the earlier review, and both commits change only `src/apu/psg.rs`. I have three minor findings:

1. `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/apu/psg.rs:498`: [minor] The doc comment on `write_tone_duty_envelope` still describes only the length load. The function now also stops a channel whose envelope is silent. Fix: add "and stops the channel when the envelope can never sound (bits 11-15 zero)".
2. `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/apu/psg.rs:477-484`: [minor] The noise channel's `SOUND4CNT_L` arm now has two steps inside the `match`, while the tone channels use a helper. It is still readable, but it is inconsistent and has no test. Fix: either add a `write_noise_envelope` helper next to `write_tone_duty_envelope`, or add one noise case to the test: a silent envelope plus a restart reads as off, and a length-byte-only write keeps it playing.
3. `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/apu/psg.rs:638`: [minor] The new test covers channel 2 only. Channel 1 and noise share the same code but are not exercised. Fix: one more assertion per channel.

**Correctness against the spec**
- **Bit positions:** the check uses mask `0xF800`, which is direction (bit 11) plus initial volume (bits 12-15). That matches gbatek SOUND1CNT_H, SOUND2CNT_L and SOUND4CNT_L.
- **Envelope running out during play:** gbatek SOUNDCNT_X says "The bits are NOT reset when an volume envelope ends." The new rule looks only at the register setting, never at the envelope's current volume, so a channel whose envelope decays to 0 still reads as on. No conflict.
- **What gbatek does not say:** gbatek only says "0=No Sound". The not-playing behaviour is not in the spec. The code comment says honestly that it comes from the mgba-io-read reference output, and CLAUDE.md allows grader outputs as a source.
- **The byte-write fix:** `io_write16` merges the write into the stored registers before the helpers run, and `PlainRegisters::read` returns the stored value unmasked. A write of only the length byte therefore checks the envelope bits that were already there, so it no longer stops a playing channel. The new test asserts exactly this. Writing a silent envelope stops the channel straight away.
- **Restart:** restarts take the envelope from the merged register, for both tone channels and noise.
- **Wave channel:** it has no envelope and still uses `SOUND3CNT_L` bit 7. That is correct.
- **Existing test:** `partial_byte_frequency_writes_merge` gained a volume-15 setup line so its restart still plays. That is a reasonable change.

**Ownership:** `src/apu/psg.rs` is APU code, which fits integrator work. No shared contract files changed.

**No per-ROM hacks:** nothing depends on a ROM's hash, title, game code or a chosen address.

**Originality:** this matches the well-known "silent envelope turns the channel off" behaviour, but the comment names a source the project allows. There are no names, structure or comments taken from another emulator, and no unexplained tables.

**Readability:** `envelope_can_sound` is a clear name with a doc comment, and the local `silent` is clear.

**Build and tests:** `cargo test` passes (126 tests) and the wasm release build succeeds. As instructed, I did not run the grader.
